bug_semantics: A user who can configure a Budibase automation can supply an arbitrary HTTP(S) URL to the outgoing-webhook (and later Zapier, n8n, Slack, Discord, and Make.com) step. The server dereferenced that URL with axios/node-fetch without destination validation, so it could reach loopback, RFC1918, link-local/cloud-metadata, and other internal services (CWE-918). The REST datasource's separate guard was also fail-open by default because an unset BLACKLIST_IPS produced an empty list and isBlacklisted returned false; it neither protected automation fetches nor supplied secure defaults.
flaw_origin: Commit 3ae82b95a31bcb6b3803d3ad8d8c5accb7606ef3 first created and registered the executable OUTGOING_WEBHOOK automation. Its run function accepted inputs.url, normalized it only by adding http://, and called axios(request) with no allowlist/denylist or resolved-address check. Commit 3d77163773d0ab37342e9e2be5d6b8797758e4eb later changed axios to node-fetch, and a3bb2e0d770fe0c66f0382aebef86faa2bbcc696 renamed/migrated the same step to TypeScript; those are implementation changes preserving the pre-existing SSRF, not introducers. Commit 564c724be11895fa6bc1766aef3a149fae3223e3 later added an opt-in REST-only blacklist whose empty-default behavior left that separate path unprotected when BLACKLIST_IPS was unset.
ai_marker: absent: raw BIC commit object has author and committer mike12345567 <me@michaeldrury.co.uk>, subject 'Adding an outgoing webhook action, so that we have both incoming and outgoing ability.', and no message trailers; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other commit-object AI marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/security/advisories/GHSA-5fpj-28rv-84r7 identifies direct fetch calls in packages/server/src/automations/steps/{outgoingWebhook,zapier,n8n,slack,discord}.ts, the empty-default packages/backend-core/src/blacklist/blacklist.ts behavior, affected <3.41.3, and patched 3.41.3.

`git log -L 63,96:packages/server/src/automations/steps/outgoingWebhook.js 3ae82b95...` resolves the complete original run function to 3ae82b95a31bcb6b3803d3ad8d8c5accb7606ef3: it reads inputs.url and calls axios(request). `git log --follow` and `git log -S'fetch(url, request)'` show 3d77163773d0ab37342e9e2be5d6b8797758e4eb as the axios-to-node-fetch change and a3bb2e0d770fe0c66f0382aebef86faa2bbcc696 as the 84%-similar JS-to-TS rename, so neither is the BIC.

Direct parent-tree check: `git ls-tree -r --name-only f9eeefb4dca55aec17f2e5088ac483cdcd257b95 -- packages/server/src/automations/steps/outgoingWebhook.js` returns no path, and that parent's packages/server/src/automations/actions.js has neither an outgoingWebhook import nor OUTGOING_WEBHOOK registration. The BIC diff creates the 96-line file and registers its run/definition, proving immediate-parent absence.

The BIC is an ordinary one-parent commit, not a merge or opaque squash: raw parents are exactly f9eeefb4dca55aec17f2e5088ac483cdcd257b95, and the vulnerable capability is directly visible as a newly created file. No decomposition was necessary.

Version membership: `git describe --contains --tags 3ae82b95...` returns v0.3.0~5^2~3; v0.2.6's actions.js lacks OUTGOING_WEBHOOK, while v0.3.0 contains the unchecked `fetch(url, request)`. Thus the BIC precedes and is present throughout the advisory's affected range.

Secondary REST lifecycle: 564c724be11895fa6bc1766aef3a149fae3223e3 created the blacklist and REST check but explicitly returned false for an empty configured list. Direct fix 62f50d9779cbd7673bc5b1d99e167f3d2e175ec1 adds hard-coded private/link-local/loopback defaults; `git describe --contains` places it in 3.33.4 (https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/commit/62f50d9779cbd7673bc5b1d99e167f3d2e175ec1).

Automation remediation: 6cfa3bcca357c56e615b93462c5e70fd81b891fc adds initial blacklist checks to every webhook step, then e7d47625be8b0e3d030a5ca5d1fd604f25098efe replaces their direct fetches with fetchWithBlacklist, which uses manual redirects and revalidates each destination (https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/commit/e7d47625be8b0e3d030a5ca5d1fd604f25098efe). Follow-ups e66be4a2b1e9301217c9bf4249b33582fc8716a5, 97fe1f1624d627878681363cf69eda1b58cb5cfc, and 37b5a63b460b14dc698a8296e9908a6480f5ad9e harden redirect handling; merge c38365d9996c2657171fd358d9aa9d2c85091c9b lands the complete branch on master (https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/commit/c38365d9996c2657171fd358d9aa9d2c85091c9b).

Boundary cross-check: `git describe --contains --tags c38365d9...` returns 3.34.2~3. Tag 3.34.1 still imports node-fetch and calls `fetch(url, request)` in outgoingWebhook.ts; tag 3.34.2 imports and calls fetchWithBlacklist. Therefore the repository history shows the automation fix by 3.34.2, before the advisory's conservative 3.41.3 patched boundary.

Advisory-boundary check: `git diff --exit-code 3.41.2..3.41.3 -- packages/server/src/automations/steps packages/backend-core/src/blacklist packages/server/src/integrations/rest.ts` is empty. Both tags already use fetchWithBlacklist and a default private-address blacklist. The 3.41.3 release reference (https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/releases/tag/3.41.3) is therefore a valid safe release but not the first repository tag containing the remediation.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p 3ae82b95a31bcb6b3803d3ad8d8c5accb7606ef3` shows only the human author/committer identity and one-line subject quoted in ai_marker, with no trailers. No PR body, branch name, later commit, or fix authorship was used for attribution.
reasoning: The attack existed as soon as the outgoing-webhook action became executable: an automation-controlled URL crossed the server trust boundary into an unrestricted HTTP client call. The later node-fetch conversion, TypeScript rename, and addition of more branded webhook steps only preserved or multiplied that same mechanism, so selecting any of those later commits would incorrectly call a refactor/extension the origin. The immediate parent lacks both the step file and its action registration, while 3ae82b95 creates both, making it the smallest real BIC available in public history. The later REST blacklist did not cure this origin because automations bypassed it, and its empty default introduced a second fail-open condition. The default-list change landed by 3.33.4; the automation branch's final redirect-aware direct fix is e7d47625, with its hardened branch landing on master at c38365d9 and appearing in 3.34.2. The advisory's stated 3.41.3 boundary is later than the actual code boundary, as 3.41.2 and 3.41.3 have no relevant diff, but this discrepancy does not prevent a closed lifecycle reconstruction. Finally, the raw BIC commit object contains only a human identity and no AI marker, so under BIC-only attribution the correct verdict is NOT_AI.
